questions.q: Why is training a Q-network directly on an agent's raw, in-order experience problematic?
options: It is too fast and finishes before enough data is collected
Consecutive states are highly correlated, violating the independent-data assumption gradient training relies on
The environment stops producing rewards
Neural networks cannot process sequential inputs at all
questions.explain: A trajectory's consecutive states are nearly identical, so training on them in order is far from the shuffled, independent data gradient-based methods assume.

questions.q: What does an experience replay buffer do?
options: Stores past transitions and samples random minibatches from them for training
Replays the exact same episode over and over
Deletes transitions immediately after they are used once
Only stores the most recent single transition
questions.explain: The replay buffer holds a history of transitions; sampling random minibatches from it decorrelates training and allows transitions to be reused.

questions.q: In the DQN loss, why does using the same network for both Q(s, a; theta) and the target cause instability?
options: It doesn't cause any instability
Because every gradient update to theta also shifts the target the network is being trained to match
Because it uses too much GPU memory
Because it requires two separate replay buffers
questions.explain: If the same weights compute both the prediction and the target, the target moves every time the weights update, so the network is chasing a constantly shifting goal.

questions.q: What is a 'hard update' of the target network?
options: Continuously blending the online network's weights into the target network every step with a small factor tau
Periodically copying the online network's weights into the target network exactly, every C steps
Retraining the target network from scratch
Freezing the online network permanently
questions.explain: A hard update copies theta into theta_minus exactly every C steps, keeping the target fixed between syncs.

questions.q: What distinguishes a Polyak (soft) update from a hard update?
options: A Polyak update happens only once at the start of training
A Polyak update blends a small fraction tau of the online weights into the target network every step, producing smoother drift instead of sudden jumps
A Polyak update deletes the replay buffer
A Polyak update is identical to a hard update but runs on the CPU
questions.explain: Soft updates nudge theta_minus toward theta by a small tau every step (theta_minus <- tau*theta + (1-tau)*theta_minus), giving continuous, gradual tracking rather than periodic exact copies.
